title: Match with Ranges
concept: Use range patterns (like 0..10) in match arms to match any value within a numeric range.
why: Ranges in match eliminate chains of if/elif for bucketed values — grades, age groups, price tiers, and more.
tips: Make sure your ranges don't overlap (or be intentional about ordering)
Use `_` after ranges to catch values outside all buckets
Ranges work great for bucketed classifications — cleaner than if/elif
common_mistakes: Overlapping ranges: `0..5` and `3..8` overlap — first one wins
Forgetting that end is exclusive: `90..100` doesn't match 100!
Using ranges for non-numeric types — ranges work with Int
